record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Quiver folding relates Coulomb branches of unfolded and folded quivers via finite-group actions, and Hilbert series and highest weight generating functions have been computed for certain non-simply laced quivers. Can one compute the Hilbert series and highest weight generating functions for the Higgs branches of folded theories?

evidence.quote: Question 5. Can we compute HS and HWGs for the Higgs branches of folded theories?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A quiver is a finite directed graph whose nodes carry compact gauge groups (typically U(n), SO(n), or Sp(n)) and whose edges encode hypermultiplet matter representations. To such a quiver one associates two hyperkähler moduli spaces: the Coulomb branch and the Higgs branch. Quiver folding is the operation of identifying nodes of a simply-laced quiver related by a discrete automorphism, producing a (generally non-simply laced) folded quiver whose Coulomb branch is the fixed-point locus of the induced action on the Coulomb branch of the unfolded quiver.

For a hyperkähler cone X with an action of a global symmetry group G, the Hilbert series HS_X(t; x) is the generating function
   HS_X(t; x) = ∑_n dim(C[X]_n) χ_n(x) t^n,
where C[X]_n is the degree-n part of the coordinate ring of X and χ_n is the character of G on this graded piece. The highest weight generating function (HWG) of X repackages this information as
   HWG_X(t; μ_1, …, μ_r) = ∑_λ a_λ(t) μ^λ,
where λ ranges over dominant weights of G, μ_i are fugacities for fundamental weights, and a_λ(t) ∈ ℤ[[t]] counts (with signs) the multiplicities of the irreducible G-representation of highest weight λ in C[X].

For non-simply laced folded quivers, the Hilbert series and HWG of the Coulomb branch have been computed in many examples via a monopole-type formula adapted to folded quivers.

Problem. Develop a systematic method to compute the Hilbert series HS and highest weight generating functions HWG of the Higgs branches of folded (non-simply laced) quiver gauge theories, and carry out these computations explicitly for natural families of such theories.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work, notably "Folding orthosymplectic quivers" (JHEP 12 (2021) 070), gives a magnetic-quiver realisation of certain Higgs branches of folded theories and computes both Coulomb and Higgs branch Hilbert series in cases where agreement can be verified, providing partial progress. A fully general, systematic prescription for HS and HWG of Higgs branches of arbitrary folded theories does not appear to be established in the literature, so the question remains partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Folding orthosymplectic quivers (JHEP 12 (2021) 070)
status_evidence.snippet: A family of folded orthosymplectic quivers is shown to be a new magnetic quiver realisation of Higgs branches of 4d N=2 theories; Coulomb and Higgs branch Hilbert series are computed and shown to agree.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on computing Higgs branch Hilbert series for folded quivers.

status_evidence.title: Ungauging schemes and Coulomb branches of non-simply laced quiver theories
status_evidence.snippet: Develops monopole formula and HS/HWG techniques for non-simply laced quivers on the Coulomb branch side.
status_evidence.claim: Coulomb-side HS/HWG for folded quivers is well developed, while Higgs side is less systematic.
